title: The Lane-Emden conjecture
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's proof (2026) of the subcritical Henon-Lane-Emden conjecture: for n >= 2, p, q > 0 and real weights A, B with (n+A)/(p+1) + (n+B)/(q+1) > n-2, the system -Laplace u = |x|^A v^p, -Laplace v = |x|^B u^q has no positive solution on R^n, continuous at the origin and twice differentiable elsewhere; for A = B = 0 this is the Lane-Emden conjecture. The first lesson proves the potential theory used (spherical means, Green representation, Liouville's theorem, Newton potentials of nonnegative supersolutions). The second reduces to n >= 3, A, B > -2, pq > 1, represents solutions as Newton potentials with estimates uniform over all solutions, and reduces the theorem by scaling to a uniform local energy bound. The third proves a localized virial identity and localizes its pressure. The fourth proves an inequality for the Newton kernel on two parallel lines and sets up weights on caps of directions and on layer intervals. The fifth integrates over lines and levels, proves the pressure estimate and the energy bound, and concludes.

checks.exact_checks: Python (scratch le_checks.py, output le_checks.out, 9 Oct 2026, 0 problems): the relations p beta = alpha + 2 + A, q alpha = beta + 2 + B and gamma = (1-a-b)(alpha+beta+2-n) for 2000 random parameter sets; the exponent arithmetic N = n^2+5n+2, 4n+7, 3n+5, 3n+8, N+2, n+1 for n = 3 to 29; the cutoff bounds on a radial grid for n = 3 to 7; the interval-pair inequality, the midpoint identity and the sign of the midpoint term by numerical integration on 250 random configurations (n = 3 to 6); cap measures against r^(n-1) by Monte Carlo (n = 3, 4, 5); the Green representation in a ball for exp(-|x|^2) in R^3 (agreement to 10 digits); the layer identity on 200 random cases; the critical solution of Exercise 6.3 of the second lesson for n = 3 to 6.

open_obligations: Existence half of the classification in Remark 5.3 of the fifth lesson: for n >= 3, A, B > -2 and (n+A)/(p+1) + (n+B)/(q+1) <= n-2 there are radial positive solutions (Bidaut-Veron and Giacomini, Theorem 1.4(i), as recorded by Phan, Proposition B). Cited, not proved in the programme, and not used in any proof of the course; the scalar critical case is checked in Exercise 6.3 of the second lesson.
